beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR addresses a mismatch between compact CTM state and dense super-resolution output.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The central issue is representation: a compact thought process has to support a dense image reconstruction task.

params.headline: Compact thought must produce a dense image field
params.sub: A super-resolution method built around a persistent dense carrier.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that the method starts from a mismatch between CTM-style compact thought and dense spatial prediction.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The comparison frames the problem before the architecture appears. CTM is compact, while super-resolution asks for spatial detail at every output location. The window-wise adaptation is a bridge, but the dense field still has to be carried through the process. DQ-CTM is the version compared for this dense-output setting.

params.headline: The compact state is not enough by itself

beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier and lets compact thought read and update it.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method keeps the dense image information alive instead of asking the thought state to hold it alone. The carrier persists through the process. The compact thought process reads from it. The same process also updates it.

params.headline: A dense carrier persists through compact thought

beats.intent: The viewer understands that the carrier is encoded from the low-resolution image and then windowed for processing.
beats.narration: The carrier is defined before the ticking process begins. The dense feature field comes from the low-resolution input. The windowed tensor is made from that dense field. The windowing step names what compact processing receives.

params.headline: The dense field is encoded and then windowed

beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR runs end to end through encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The end-to-end diagram turns the carrier idea into a concrete path. The encoder creates the feature field. The windows organize that field for compact processing. The shared DQ-CTM ticks refine it over time. The decoder converts the result back into a super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR routes dense features through shared ticks

beats.intent: The viewer understands where the encoder, windows, shared ticks, and decoder are represented in the end-to-end figure.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The figure shows the same path as a system diagram. The encoder is the entry point from the low-resolution image. Windowing gives the dense field a local processing structure. The DQ-CTM block is shared across ticks rather than replaced each time. The decoder is where the dense result becomes the reconstructed image.

params.headline: The repeated block is shared across ticks

beats.intent: The viewer understands that reconstruction is shown over ticks from T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.claim: Reconstruction at T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.narration: The progress figure makes the ticking process visible as reconstruction states. Bicubic provides the non-ThinkSR reference. The sequence then shows outputs from T equals zero through T equals four. Ground truth anchors what the reconstruction is trying to match.

params.headline: Reconstruction is tracked across T equals zero through four

beats.intent: The viewer understands that absolute-error maps compare the same crops using one shared color scale.
beats.claim: Absolute-error maps on the same crops, one shared colour scale.
beats.narration: The error maps switch from appearance to absolute error. The crops match the reconstruction examples. A single color scale keeps the maps comparable. That shared scale matters because each crop is judged on the same error encoding.

params.headline: The error maps use the same crops and scale

beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR is competitive with CNN baselines but trails recent lightweight transformers.
beats.claim: Competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: The reported result is mixed rather than one-sided. DQ-CTM-SR is close to the CNN baselines in the table. CATANet is the recent lightweight transformer result ahead of it. The conclusion is competitive with CNNs, but not with the strongest listed lightweight transformer.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is close to CNN baselines but behind CATANet

beats.intent: The viewer understands that DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest listed method, even though it is below CARN in parameters.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR: 1.129M params; CARN: 1.592M; IMDN: 0.715M; RFDN: 0.550M; CATANet: 0.535M.
beats.narration: The parameter column gives the cost side of the result. DQ-CTM-SR uses fewer parameters than CARN. It uses more parameters than IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet. CATANet is both the smallest listed model and the highest average scorer.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is smaller than CARN but larger than the others

beats.intent: The viewer understands the exact benchmark rows behind the score and parameter comparisons.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The table is the source for both the score comparison and the size comparison. RFDN is the closest CNN-row average above DQ-CTM-SR. CATANet is the highest average in the table. DQ-CTM-SR is reported at 1.129 million parameters and 28.983 average.

params.headline: The table reports size and average score together

beats.intent: The viewer understands the tradeoff: ThinkSR supplies a dense carrier for compact thought, with results that are plausible but not state of the art in the listed table.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process; competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: ThinkSR's contribution is the carrier that lets compact thought operate on a dense reconstruction problem. The reported outcome is competitive with CNN baselines, while the listed lightweight transformer remains ahead.

params.headline: The carrier solves the mismatch, but not the full benchmark gap
